limitations: The package has never run on a physical player: the admission cases speak to a fake local Control API over loopback HTTP, and no packaged build has been installed on a device.

A packaged Sonos is a remote, not the built-in player screen. The four declarative component kinds carry transport commands, relative volume, mute and a source picker; they cannot carry album artwork, a seek bar or position clocks, a volume meter, shuffle, repeat or crossfade state, the queue, or any group and coordinator awareness.
Playback is refused on a group member as in the built-in client, but the package cannot say which coordinator to open: the protocol carries nine fixed error codes and no message of its own.
Status is read on demand rather than polled, so a change made from the Sonos app does not appear until the next command or an explicit refresh.
The source picker loses its second line, because Selectable carries an id and a name only, and the current source is never highlighted because a player does not report which favourite it is playing.
No now-playing text is reported: filling the status title would cost an extra household read on every status request, and one free-form field cannot hold track, artist and album separately.

The developer API key is a per-connection secret setting. A packaged build carries none, because the feed's build job has no secrets and the host clears the child's environment, so a connection without a key falls back to the documented placeholder and works only on players that allow guest access.

hardware_validation.notes: The couch-sonos client has been exercised against real players on the LAN, but this package adapter, its manifest and its plugin binary have not: every admission case runs against a fake Control API on loopback. Packaged hardware validation remains outstanding, so the entry stays preview and not-tested.
